evidence_items.explanation: NEWTON found uneven physical-attribute performance and identified a scenario where GPT-4 struggled to answer consistently. Its 87.7% average across scenario tasks is substantial counterweight: the result supports incomplete reliability, not general physical-reasoning incapacity.

GPT-4-0314 scored 97.5% on the original false-belief category but 0% on two altered unexpected-transfer categories. These sharp differences support unreliable transfer across psychological scenarios, while the original-task success limits any claim of general incapacity.

GSM-Plus tested GPT-4 among models solving original grade-school problems and controlled variations; successful original answers did not consistently transfer to altered problems. Multiple prompting methods improved performance but did not produce consistent robustness across the tested variations.

This study found GPT-4 matched or exceeded humans on several theory-of-mind tests, with weakness concentrated in faux-pas detection. Follow-up experiments attributed that weakness to excessive caution, cautioning against interpreting every wrong answer as an inability to infer mental states.
